question: What is the primary focus of health education within primary health care?

options.A: Empowering individuals to manage their own well-being
options.B: Increasing government revenue from health services
options.C: Replacing traditional healers with orthodox clinics
options.D: Reducing the administrative workload of hospital staff

explanation: Health education equips people with the knowledge and skills needed to make informed health decisions independently. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why do nurses play a vital role in community health instruction?

options.A: They focus solely on hospital-based surgical interventions
options.B: They have exclusive authority to distribute government medication
options.C: They translate complex medical concepts into culturally accessible messages
options.D: They dictate strict health routines that communities must follow

explanation: Effective public health instruction requires bridging the gap between clinical science and local understanding. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which demographic group experiences the highest morbidity from endemic malaria in Nigeria?

options.A: Young adult males in corporate employment
options.B: Teenage school students in rural areas
options.C: Children under five and pregnant women

explanation: Immune vulnerability makes young children and pregnant women exceptionally susceptible to severe malaria complications. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h2)

question: An increase in hypertension and type 2 diabetes across Nigerian urban centers is primarily linked to what factor?

options.A: Shifts toward sedentary urban lifestyles and dietary changes
options.B: Widespread genetic mutations specific to city dwellers
options.C: Mandatory physical training programs in workplaces
options.D: Complete eradication of traditional herbal remedies

explanation: Urbanization often brings processed diets and reduced physical activity, accelerating non-communicable disease rates. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h2)

question: According to the Health Belief Model, what must a person perceive before taking preventive health action?

options.A: Personal vulnerability and severity of the condition
options.B: Guaranteed financial compensation from the hospital
options.C: Immediate elimination of all environmental risks

explanation: Individuals only act when they feel genuinely at risk and understand the serious consequences of inaction. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is understanding the stages of the Transtheoretical Model important for nurses?

options.A: It provides a formula for calculating community disease incidence
options.B: It eliminates the need for any follow-up clinical assessments
options.C: It allows tailoring educational interventions to the patient's current readiness level
options.D: It accurately predicts the exact date a patient will stop smoking

explanation: A person in the precontemplation stage requires a very different teaching approach than someone already ready for action. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the mandatory first step when planning a community-based health education program?

options.A: Renting a large auditorium in the state capital
options.C: Conducting a comprehensive community needs assessment
options.D: Drafting mandatory enforcement policies for local chiefs

explanation: Interventions must address real, community-identified problems rather than perceived external priorities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h4)

question: A nurse plans a health talk on exclusive breastfeeding in an agrarian Nigerian community. When is the best time to schedule this session to ensure high attendance?

options.A: Early Monday morning when everyone is traveling away
options.B: During off-peak farming seasons or local market days
options.C: Mid-morning during the peak planting and harvesting season
options.D: At midnight when all farm work has completely finished

explanation: Aligning educational sessions with community rhythms and gathering times guarantees maximum participation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which teaching method is most effective for ensuring learners acquire a physical skill like preparing oral rehydration salt solution?
explanation: Demonstrations allow learners to observe, practice, and master physical health procedures hands-on. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why should nurses avoid heavy medical jargon during community health education sessions?

options.A: It violates international nursing licensing laws
options.B: It proves that the nurse lacks clinical training
options.C: It alienates listeners and hinders clear comprehension
options.D: It causes immediate physical exhaustion in the audience

explanation: Plain language and local dialects ensure that messages resonate and are easily understood by all community members. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h5)

question: How should a nurse respond when cultural myths contradict vital health education messages?

options.A: Publicly ridicule individuals who express traditional beliefs
options.B: Refuse to provide any further medical care to the village
options.C: Ignore the myths entirely and repeat the clinical lecture louder
options.D: Engage respected community and religious figures with empathy to address the misconceptions

explanation: Collaborating with trusted local leaders helps challenge harmful myths respectfully and effectively. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical barrier to behavioral change in community health?

options.B: Guaranteed financial stability and abundant clean water
options.C: Severe economic poverty and lack of resources

explanation: Abundant resources and financial stability facilitate health choices rather than acting as barriers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary difference between monitoring and evaluation in health education?

options.A: Monitoring only happens after the project is completely finished
options.B: Monitoring is continuous during implementation, while evaluation assesses outcomes at milestones or completion
options.C: Evaluation focuses exclusively on counting how many chairs were rented
options.D: Monitoring requires laboratory blood tests, while evaluation does not

explanation: Monitoring tracks daily progress, whereas evaluation measures the final impact and achievement of objectives. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h7)

question: A clinic nurse wants to evaluate whether a community education campaign on immunizations was successful six months later. Which indicator should be reviewed?

options.A: The number of printed flyers left in the storage room
options.B: The total cost of refreshments served at the opening meeting
options.C: An increase in vaccine uptake rates at local health facilities
options.D: How many hours the nurse spent preparing lecture notes

explanation: True educational success is reflected in measurable behavioral shifts, such as higher immunization coverage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h7)
